## Orientation

Territory: this wave is alone. Write only `/home/andrewyin/se-workflow--evidence-view/dashboard/model.py` and `/home/andrewyin/se-workflow--evidence-view/tests/test_dashboard_model.py`. Do not edit `dashboard/app.py`, `dashboard/tasks.py`, `dashboard/task_detail.py`, or add `dashboard/requirement_detail.py`. Later waves read these types and must not need a model change.

The worktree is the git checkout. The primary checkout `/home/andrewyin/se-workflow` holds the store. Do not edit `.artifacts/` anywhere. Do not call `adaptive-artifacts` against the project store. Tests seed temp stores through `tests/helpers.py` and `conftest.py` the way `tests/test_dashboard_model.py` already does. Run pytest from the worktree:

`uv run --with textual --with pytest python -m pytest tests/test_dashboard_model.py -q -k evidence`

then the whole model file. Write each new test first and see it fail before implementing that behavior.

A shell function named `adaptive-artifacts` points at `~/.artifacts/se-workflow`, which is not this repo. Tests must keep using the helper CLI against the temp store.

Default new fields so existing `PhaseRow`, `NeedsYouItem`, and `EffortView` constructors in tests keep working. `NEEDS_ORDER` becomes `blocking-question`, `loop-route`, `integration`, then the current kinds. Specification is listed with `--full`. A CLI error on specification, design, assessment, integration-report, or release becomes an empty list, not `ModelError`. Other types still raise.

`PhaseEvidence.decisions` is each design decision's subject and choice. The design payload `decisions` is comma-separated subjects; join `project:decision` (that type is not one of the five soft-fail types). `non_goals` is the specification `## Non-goals` text. `integration` carries the latest report's result and its `## Conflicts` text. Requirement text is the `R<n>: text` line under `## Requirements`.

Stage loop order for earliest `next`: specify, design, plan, execute, integrate, verify, release. `assess` is only the final fallback. Rule 2 applies when any latest assessment is not `verified`. Rule 3 applies when every requirement id has a latest assessment of `verified`. Rules 4–9 apply when some requirement is still unassessed (or there is no assessment) and no non-verified assessment took rule 2. `derived.wave` on the work-item is the wave. A passing integration-report has `result` `pass`. The latest report is the newest `recorded_at`. The latest release is the active `project:release` for that phase; `state` `ready` sets `release_ready` on that phase's evidence and on `EffortView`. Do not change `finished`.

Needs you, latest assessment only: `loop-route` when `next` is specify, design, or plan, or `status` is `blocked`, or `confidence` is `low` and the route is not execute, verify, or insufficient. No item for `next` execute, `next` verify with a status other than `blocked`, or `status` insufficient. `integration` only for the latest report when `result` is `fail` or `blocked`. Put `phase` and `requirement` on `NeedsYouItem` (requirement empty for an integration item).

Activity uses the existing recent window. Assessment summary names requirement, status, and next, and marks an upstream route (`next` in specify, design, plan) and a level change against the previous superseded assessment for that requirement. `failed` when an assessment status is `failed` or `blocked`, an integration result is `fail` or `blocked`, or a release state is `failed`.

`load_requirement_detail` lists superseded assessments (`list --state superseded`) plus the active one, oldest first. Decisions there are the traced tasks' payload `decisions` resolved to subject and choice. Acceptances in the phase whose `requirement` is the id, each with its latest check-run and that check-run's `evidence_kind`.

## Requirements

R1: A structured phase's header row in the task table shows `R n/m verified`, where m is the number of ids in its specification and n is how many have a latest assessment of `verified`.
R2: Phase detail of a structured phase lists each requirement with its id, status, next stage, and the number of work-items whose `requirements` include it. Status is the latest assessment's status, or `unassessed` with the latest check-run result for that requirement shown dimmed.
R3: Enter on a requirement opens a requirement detail screen showing the requirement text from the specification, the decisions of the tasks traced to it, the traced tasks and acceptances, the latest check-run per acceptance with its evidence kind, and every assessment for it oldest first with status, level, next, and confidence. Enter on a traced task opens its task detail; esc returns one screen at a time.
R5: Phase detail of a structured phase shows the stage strip specify, design, plan, execute, integrate, verify, assess, release with the current stage marked, the specification weight and non-goals, the design decisions, and the latest integration-report result with its conflicts. The stepper's current phase shows the current stage word.
R6: Needs you lists each requirement whose latest assessment has `next` of specify, design, or plan, a status of `blocked`, or `confidence` `low`, and each phase whose latest integration-report is `fail` or `blocked`. Enter on an assessment item opens the requirement detail; enter on an integration item opens the Needs-you detail.
R7: A latest release with state `ready` shows a Release ready badge on the effort and on its phase. The derived "finished" rule does not change.
R8: Activity lists assessments (requirement, status, next, marked when the route goes upstream or the level escalates), integration-reports, and releases. Failed and blocked ones use the error colour.
R9: A phase with no specification, and incidental work, render exactly as before: no tally, strip, stage word, badge, or new Needs-you item.
R10: A store whose contract lacks any evidence-loop type loads with no error and renders as before.

## Invariants

Status comes only from the latest assessment for that phase and id. Requirement identity is phase plus id. A phase with no specification takes every existing code path unchanged. The dashboard stays read-only.

## Assumptions

Requirement text parses from `R<n>: text` lines under `## Requirements`. Comma-separated `requirements` and `decisions` payloads split on commas with whitespace trimmed. A check-run's phase comes from its acceptance through `criterion_id`. `list --state superseded` returns earlier assessments.

## Decisions

evidence-under-phase: Requirements live under their phase: a tally on the phase header, a list in phase detail, and a requirement detail screen.
evidence-view-scope: One phase covers the requirement view, trace links, Needs-you triggers, the stage strip, the release badge, and activity lines.
unassessed-requirement-status: A requirement with no assessment shows unassessed with the latest check-run result dimmed.
loop-needs-you-triggers: Needs you shows latest assessments that route to specify, design, or plan, are blocked, or have low confidence, and failed or blocked integration-reports.
release-ready-badge: A ready release shows a Release ready badge on the effort and its phase; the derived finished rule is unchanged.
stage-strip-placement: The full stage strip is in phase detail; the stepper shows only the current stage word.
